mainTopic: Which offerings need הגשה, תנופה, both or neither, and how and where these rites are done
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא on the פסוק 'וְהִגִּישָׁהּ'. It concludes that a מנחה needs הגשה only if part of it is burned on the altar, it comes on its own, and part of it is eaten by the כהנים. That rule leaves out שתי הלחם, לחם הפנים, מנחת נסכים, מנחת כהנים and מנחת כהן משיח. A גזירה שוה from 'בְּקֻמְצוֹ' then shows that the קמיצה is done with the כהן's hand, not with a כלי. Next comes a new משנה that sorts offerings into groups: those that need only תנופה, those that need both תנופה and הגשה, and those that need neither. The משנה also explains how the waving is done, that waving is in the east and הגשה in the west, and that waving comes first. רבי שמעון adds that שלמי יחיד, שלמי ציבור and אשם מצורע each get two of three מצוות: סמיכה, תנופה while alive, and תנופה after שחיטה. The גמרא learns that the מצורע's אשם and לוג are ideally waved together, though separately also works, and only once. It also explains why 'לפני ה׳' can mean the east. Finally, it shows that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learns waving for ביכורים through a גזירה שוה of 'hand' from שלמים.

steps.title: Ordinary meal offerings are included; the libation meal offering is excluded
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that all ordinary מנחות need הגשה because they are brought on their own. The מנחת נסכים is left out because it only comes along with an animal קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include the other meal offerings, which come on their own account. I exclude the libation meal offering, which does not come on its own account.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is answering an earlier question: which מנחות are included in the rule of הגשה? It includes the ones that come on their own and leaves out the מנחת נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test here is whether the מנחה is a קרבן in its own right. The מנחת נסכים is only an add-on to an animal offering, so it does not get the הגשה requirement. This test will be challenged right away.

keyTerms.meaning: I include (in the rule)
I exclude (from the rule)
The flour offering brought together with an animal קרבן and its wine
On their own account, as a stand-alone offering
Bringing the מנחה near to the corner of the altar

phrases.english: I include the other meal offerings
which come on their own account,
phrases.notes: He means they are brought by themselves, not as an add-on to an animal sacrifice.

phrases.english: and I exclude the libation meal offering
which does not come on its own account.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְרַבֶּה אֲנִי שְׁאָר מְנָחוֹת שֶׁבָּאוֹת בִּגְלַל עַצְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question from earlier in the ברייתא (before this section) about which מנחות are included.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Stand-alone מנחות need הגשה; the מנחת נסכים does not.

steps.title: Challenge: the priests' meal offerings also come on their own
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges itself. מנחת כהנים and מנחת כהן משיח also come on their own, so by the test just given they should need הגשה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the priests' meal offering and the anointed priest's meal offering also come on their own account. So I might think they too require bringing near?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tests the rule it just gave and finds a problem. By the 'comes on its own' test, the priests' מנחות should be included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test from step 1 seems too wide. It would include מנחת כהנים and מנחת כהן משיח, and the ברייתא assumes these do not need הגשה. So either the test is incomplete or a פסוק must exclude them.

keyTerms.meaning: A meal offering brought by a regular כהן; it is burned completely
The daily meal offering of the כהן גדול; it is also burned completely
One might think (introduces a possibility that will be rejected)
But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But the meal offering of priests
and the meal offering of the anointed priest
come on their own account,
so might they require bringing near?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא מִנְחַת כֹּהֲנִים וּמִנְחַת כֹּהֵן מָשִׁיחַ בָּאוֹת בִּגְלַל עַצְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the test given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'comes on its own' test from step 1
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The test would also include the priests' מנחות, which should be excluded.

steps.title: The word 'וְהִגִּישָׁהּ' excludes the priests' offerings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that the פסוק says 'וְהִגִּישָׁהּ', 'and he shall bring IT near'. This wording narrows the rule and leaves out the priests' מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And he shall bring it near.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the challenge with a פסוק. The word 'it' limits who needs הגשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The priests' מנחות are not excluded by logic. They are excluded by the wording of the פסוק. This immediately raises a new problem, because that same word seems to be needed for the basic rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches / therefore the verse says
And he shall bring it near (ויקרא 2:8)

phrases.english: The verse states: "And he shall bring it near."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:8. The word 'it' is read as narrowing the rule, which leaves out the priests' offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The priests' מנחות should need הגשה because they come on their own.

steps.title: Challenge: that word is needed for the basic rule of bringing near
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא objects that 'וְהִגִּישָׁהּ' is the very source that a מנחה needs הגשה at all. So how can it also be used to exclude something?
steps.simpleTranslation: But this word is needed for its own purpose, to teach that a meal offering requires bringing near!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges the answer in step 3. The word is already used for something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word that teaches the basic law cannot also teach an exclusion unless there is something extra in it. The challenge asks where that extra is.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (another purpose)
For its own basic teaching

phrases.english: But this is needed for its own purpose,
that a meal offering requires bringing near!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source used in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using 'וְהִגִּישָׁהּ' to exclude the priests' מנחות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word is already needed to teach the basic requirement of הגשה.

steps.title: The extra letter teaches the exclusion
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the פסוק could have said 'וְהִגִּישׁ'. Saying 'וְהִגִּישָׁהּ', with the extra 'it', gives room for the exclusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the difference between 'and he shall bring' and 'and he shall bring it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows that the word does two jobs. The basic word teaches הגשה, and the extra letter teaches the exclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וְהִגִּישׁ' alone would teach the basic rule. The added 'ה', meaning 'it', is extra, and it limits the rule. So both teachings come from the same word.

keyTerms.meaning: From 'and he brought' to 'and he brought it': the extra letter is learned from

steps.whatToRemember: One word can teach two things: the basic rule comes from the main word, and the extra letter limits who the rule applies to.

phrases.english: From "and he shall bring" to "and he shall bring it."
phrases.notes: The פסוק could have just said 'וְהִגִּישׁ'; the extra letter at the end is what teaches the exclusion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word is used up by the basic rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The basic word teaches the rule, and the extra 'ה' teaches the exclusion.

steps.title: Why include some offerings and exclude the priests' offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know which way the limiting word works. Why include ordinary מנחות and leave out מנחת כהנים and מנחת כהן משיח, and not the other way around?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see to include the other meal offerings and to exclude the priests' meal offering and the anointed priest's meal offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks for a reason behind the split. This sets up a clearer test in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limiting word tells us that some מנחות are excluded, but not which ones. The ברייתא needs a logical reason for drawing the line where it did.

keyTerms.meaning: And what did you see (what is your reason) to decide this way?

phrases.english: And what did you see to include the other meal offerings,
and to exclude the meal offering of priests
and the meal offering of the anointed priest?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the exclusion established in steps 3 to 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logical basis for which מנחות are included and which are excluded.

steps.title: The full test: part burned on the altar, part eaten by the priests
steps.stepSummary: A מנחה needs הגשה only if three things are true: part of it is burned on the altar, it comes on its own, and part of it is eaten by the כהנים. Each excluded offering is missing one of these.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include the other meal offerings, since part of them goes to the altar fire, they come on their own, and part of them goes to the priests. I exclude the two loaves and the showbread, since no part of them goes to the fire. I exclude the libation meal offering, since it does not come on its own. And I exclude the priests' meal offering and the anointed priest's meal offering, since no part of them goes to the priests.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a complete test for which מנחות need הגשה. It then shows why each excluded offering fails the test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים are not burned on the altar at all. מנחת נסכים is only an add-on to another קרבן. מנחת כהנים and מנחת כהן משיח are burned completely, so the כהנים eat nothing from them. Only ordinary מנחות have all three features.

keyTerms.meaning: To the fires, meaning burned on the altar
The two loaves offered on שבועות
The showbread placed on the שולחן each שבת
Part of them is eaten by the כהנים

steps.whatToRemember: הגשה applies only to a מנחה that (1) has a part burned on the altar, (2) comes on its own, and (3) has a part eaten by the כהנים.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two exclusions. שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים have nothing burned on the altar, while the priests' מנחות are the opposite: everything is burned and nothing is eaten.

phrases.english: I include the other meal offerings,
since part of them goes to the fires,
and they come on their own account,
and part of them goes to the priests.

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹצִיא אֲנִי שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם וְלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים,
phrases.english: And I exclude the two loaves and the showbread,
since no part of them goes to the fires.
And I exclude the libation meal offering,
which does not come on its own account.
And I exclude the priests' meal offering and the anointed priest's meal offering,
since no part of them goes to the priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְרַבֶּה אֲנִי שְׁאָר מְנָחוֹת, שֶׁיֵּשׁ מֵהֶן לָאִישִּׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Included מנחות have a part for the altar, come on their own, and have a part for the כהנים; every excluded offering lacks one of these.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for which מנחות are brought to the corner of the altar before the קמיצה.

steps.title: Could the removal of the handful be done with a vessel?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא moves on to the next word in the פסוק, 'וְהֵרִים' (ויקרא 2:9). It suggests that perhaps the כהן may take off the portion using a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he shall take off': might it be done with a vessel?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא opens a new topic: how the הרמה is done. It raises a possibility that will be rejected in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וְהֵרִים' by itself does not say how the portion is removed. So one might think a utensil is allowed. The next step uses another פסוק to rule this out.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall take off (lift out) the portion
With a vessel or utensil

phrases.english: "And he shall take off": might it be with a vessel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next word of the same פסוק section; a new topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הרמה may be done with a vessel.

steps.title: Learned from another verse: it must be done with the hand
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings 'וְהֵרִים מִמֶּנּוּ בְּקֻמְצוֹ' (ויקרא 6:8). Through a comparison of the same word, it shows that the הרמה in ויקרא 2 must also be done with the כהן's hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And he shall take off from it with his handful.' Just as the taking off stated there is with his handful, so too the taking off stated here is with his handful.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the idea of using a vessel. It links the two פסוקים that both use the word 'הרמה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים use the word for 'taking off'. The one in ויקרא 6 says outright that it is done 'with his handful'. So the same requirement carries over to ויקרא 2, and a כלי is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: With his handful, using his own hand
Just as ... so too (the form of a comparison)
There (the other פסוק) ... here (this פסוק)
The taking off of the portion

steps.whatToRemember: The הרמה of a מנחה must be done with the כהן's own hand, not with a vessel. This is learned from 'בְּקֻמְצוֹ' in ויקרא 6:8.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And he shall take off from it with his handful,"
just as the taking off stated there is with his handful,
so too the taking off stated here is with his handful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the possibility raised in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הרמה must be done with the hand, learned by comparing the two פסוקים.

steps.title: Offerings that need waving but not bringing near
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the offerings that need תנופה but not הגשה: the מצורע's לוג of oil and his אשם, ביכורים according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, the אימורים and חזה ושוק of a private שלמים, and the two loaves and two lambs of עצרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: These offerings must be waved but do not need to be brought near the altar: the לוג of oil of a מצורע and his guilt offering, the ביכורים (according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב), the altar parts of a private peace offering together with its breast and thigh (for both men and women, by Jews and not by others), and the two loaves with the two lambs of שבועות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It gives a list of offerings that are waved (תנופה) but are not brought near to the altar (הגשה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the sugya dealt with הגשה, an action done mainly with מנחות. This משנה introduces a second action, תנופה, and shows that the two do not always go together. All the items here, including animal parts, oil and fruit, are waved, but none of them gets הגשה.

keyTerms.meaning: Waving: moving the offering back and forth and up and down before ה׳
Bringing near: carrying a מנחה up to the corner of the altar
The measure of oil brought by a recovered מצורע together with his אשם
The parts of an animal offering that are burned on the altar
The breast and thigh of a שלמים, which are given to the כהן
The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות (עצרת)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume every offering that is waved is also brought near. This משנה deliberately separates the two actions. Each one has its own list.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
These require waving
and do not require bringing near:
the log of oil of a recovered leper,
and his guilt offering,
phrases.notes: This is the מצורע's own אשם, which is waved together with the oil.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַבִּכּוּרִים כְּדִבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: and the first fruits, according to the words of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov,
and the altar portions of an individual's peace offerings,
and their breast and thigh.
Both men and women,
by Jews and not by others.
The two loaves and the two lambs of Shavuot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלּוּ טְעוּנוֹת תְּנוּפָה וְאֵין טְעוּנוֹת הַגָּשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה. It moves from the earlier discussion of הגשה to the parallel action of תנופה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מצורע's log and אשם, ביכורים (per רבי אליעזר בן יעקב), the אימורים and חזה ושוק of a private שלמים, and the two loaves and lambs of עצרת need תנופה but not הגשה.

steps.title: How the waving is done
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the waving of the two loaves and two lambs. The loaves go on top of the lambs, the כהן's hands go underneath, and he moves them forward and back and up and down, based on the פסוק 'אשר הונף ואשר הורם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is the waving done? He puts the two loaves on top of the two lambs and places both hands underneath. He moves them out and back, and lifts them up and down, as the פסוק says: 'which was waved and which was raised.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the actual movements of תנופה, using the two loaves and two lambs of שבועות as the example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תנופה has two motions. One is horizontal, out and back (מוליך ומביא). The other is vertical, up and down (מעלה ומוריד). The משנה gets both from the double phrase in the פסוק: 'הונף' is the waving and 'הורם' is the raising.

keyTerms.meaning: Moves it out and brings it back (the horizontal motion)
Raises and lowers (the vertical motion)
Was waved
Was raised

phrases.english: How does he do it?
He places the two loaves
on top of the two lambs,
and puts his two hands underneath,
moves them out and brings them back,
raises and lowers them,
as it is stated: "Which was waved and which was raised."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After listing what needs תנופה, the משנה explains how תנופה is physically done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנופה is done with the hands underneath, moving out and back and up and down, learned from 'אשר הונף ואשר הורם'.

steps.title: Where waving and bringing near take place, and which comes first
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says תנופה was done on the east side and הגשה on the west side, and that waving always comes before bringing near.
steps.simpleTranslation: Waving was done in the east, and bringing near in the west. Wavings come before bringings near.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two practical rules. The first says where each action is done. The second says which action is done first when an offering needs both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The location rule shows that the two actions are separate rites done in different places. The order rule matters for offerings that need both, which the משנה lists next: such an offering is waved first and only afterward brought near.

keyTerms.meaning: On the east side
On the west side
Come first, take precedence

phrases.english: Waving was in the east,
and bringing near was in the west.
Wavings come before bringings near.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the location and order of תנופה compared with הגשה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנופה is done in the east and הגשה in the west. תנופה comes before הגשה.

steps.title: Offerings that need both, and offerings that need neither
steps.stepSummary: The מנחת העומר and the מנחת קנאות need both הגשה and תנופה. The לחם הפנים and the מנחת נסכים need neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: The עומר offering and the סוטה's jealousy offering need both bringing near and waving. The showbread and the meal offering that comes with wine offerings need neither bringing near nor waving.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its sorting. It names two מנחות that need both actions and two that need neither.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה now covers every combination: only waving (step 10), only bringing near (the earlier discussion), both, and neither. The מנחת העומר and the מנחת קנאות get both actions, waving first, as step 12 taught. The לחם הפנים and the מנחת נסכים get no special handling of either kind.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the second day of פסח
The 'jealousy' meal offering of a סוטה
The showbread placed on the שולחן each שבת
The meal offering brought along with the wine of an animal offering

steps.whatToRemember: Four groups: only תנופה (the מצורע's לוג and אשם, ביכורים, private שלמים, the two loaves and lambs); both (עומר, קנאות); neither (לחם הפנים, נסכים). Waving is in the east and bringing near in the west, and waving comes first.

phrases.english: The omer meal offering and the meal offering of jealousy
require bringing near and waving.
The showbread and the libation meal offering

phrases.aramaic: אֵין טְעוּנוֹת לֹא הַגָּשָׁה וְלֹא תְּנוּפָה.
phrases.english: require neither bringing near nor waving.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנְחַת הָעוֹמֶר וּמִנְחַת קְנָאוֹת טְעוּנוֹת הַגָּשָׁה וּתְנוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה's sorting by adding the 'both' and 'neither' groups.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מנחת העומר and מנחת קנאות need both הגשה and תנופה. The לחם הפנים and מנחת נסכים need neither.

steps.title: Three offerings that each need two of three מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says three kinds of offerings each need two out of three מצוות, and each one is missing the third. The three are שלמי יחיד, שלמי ציבור, and אשם מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: three types of offerings require three מצוות. Each one gets two of them, and the third is not done with it. They are: an individual's peace offerings, the community's peace offerings, and the מצורע's guilt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a general rule about three offerings. This sets up the next line, where he explains which two מצוות each one gets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three מצוות in play: סמיכה, תנופה while the animal is alive, and תנופה after it is slaughtered. Each offering gets two of them, but not the same two. This step only names the offerings; the details come next.

keyTerms.meaning: Types or kinds (here, kinds of offerings)
Peace offerings brought by one person
Peace offerings of the community (the two lambs of עצרת)
The guilt offering a healed מצורע brings

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: three types
require three מצוות,
two of them in each and every one,
and the third is not done with them.
And these are they: an individual's peace offerings,
the community's peace offerings, and the metzora's guilt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: שְׁלֹשָׁה מִינִין טְעוּנִין שָׁלֹשׁ מִצְוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's lists of which offerings need תנופה and הגשה, now adding סמיכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three offerings each require two of the three מצוות (סמיכה, live תנופה, slaughtered תנופה), and each one lacks a different one.

steps.title: Which two מצוות each offering gets
steps.stepSummary: שלמי יחיד get סמיכה while alive and תנופה after שחיטה. שלמי ציבור get תנופה both alive and slaughtered, with no סמיכה. אשם מצורע gets סמיכה and תנופה while alive, with no תנופה after שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: An individual's peace offerings need hand-leaning while alive and waving after slaughter, but no waving while alive. The community's peace offerings need waving both alive and slaughtered, but no hand-leaning. The מצורע's guilt offering needs hand-leaning and waving while alive, but no waving after slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון now fills in his rule and tells us exactly which two מצוות each offering gets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each offering is missing a different מצוה. שלמי יחיד lack live תנופה, שלמי ציבור lack סמיכה, and אשם מצורע lacks תנופה after שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaning one's hands on the animal's head before slaughter
Waving the offering
While still alive
After being slaughtered

steps.whatToRemember: שלמי יחיד: סמיכה plus slaughtered תנופה. שלמי ציבור: live and slaughtered תנופה, no סמיכה. אשם מצורע: סמיכה plus live תנופה.

phrases.aramaic: זִבְחֵי שַׁלְמֵי יָחִיד – טְעוּנִין סְמִיכָה חַיִּים,
phrases.english: An individual's peace offerings require hand-leaning while alive,
and waving once slaughtered,
but they have no waving while alive.
The community's peace offerings
require waving both alive and slaughtered,
[but they have no hand-leaning].
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording; some versions don't have them. They fit the pattern of naming the one מצוה that's missing.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲשַׁם מְצוֹרָע – טָעוּן סְמִיכָה וּתְנוּפָה חַי,
phrases.english: And the metzora's guilt offering requires hand-leaning and waving while alive,
but it has no waving once slaughtered.

steps.triggerLanguage: זִבְחֵי שַׁלְמֵי יָחִיד – טְעוּנִין סְמִיכָה חַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the details of the rule stated in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of the three offerings has a different combination of סמיכה and live or slaughtered תנופה.

steps.title: The metzora's guilt offering and oil are waved together
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the plural word 'אותם' in the פסוק that the מצורע's אשם and לוג of oil are waved together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: 'And he shall offer it as a guilt offering, and the לוג of oil, and wave them as a wave offering.' This teaches that they need waving together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a ברייתא that explains where the משנה's waving of the אשם מצורע comes from. It shows the oil and the animal are waved as one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'והניף אותם', 'wave them', in the plural. So it is talking about both items at once, and the ideal way is to wave them together.

keyTerms.meaning: The measure of oil the מצורע brings
Together, as one
This teaches

phrases.english: GEMARA. The Rabbis taught:
"And he shall offer it as a guilt offering
and the log of oil,
and wave them as a wave offering"
phrases.notes: The key word is 'them', which means both the animal and the oil.

phrases.english: this teaches that they require waving together.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וְהִקְרִיב אֹתוֹ לְאָשָׁם וְאֶת לֹג הַשָּׁמֶן וְהֵנִיף אֹתָם תְּנוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא, giving the source for the waving of the אשם מצורע and its oil mentioned in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אשם מצורע and the לוג of oil are ideally waved together.

steps.title: What if each was waved separately
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know that waving the אשם and the oil separately still works.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that if he waved this one by itself and that one by itself, he has fulfilled his obligation?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks for a source that separate waving is also valid. This sets up the answer in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 taught that the ideal is to wave them together. Now the question is whether together is required, or whether waving each alone is still acceptable after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: By itself
He has fulfilled his obligation

phrases.english: And from where do we know that if he waved
this one by itself and that one by itself, he has fulfilled his obligation?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם הֵנִיף זֶה בְּעַצְמוֹ וְזֶה בְּעַצְמוֹ יָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the 'together' rule from step 16 is only the ideal.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that waving the אשם and the oil separately is valid.

steps.title: The singular words show separate waving works
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא points to the singular words 'אותו לאשם והניף', which speak about the אשם alone, so it may be waved by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And he shall offer it as a guilt offering and wave.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question by reading the same פסוק a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beginning of the פסוק talks about 'it', the אשם alone, together with 'and wave'. That shows the אשם can be waved on its own. So waving together is the ideal, and waving separately still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (introduces the proof from the פסוק)

phrases.english: The verse says
"And he shall offer it as a guilt offering and wave."
phrases.notes: Here the ברייתא reads 'it', just the animal, right next to 'and wave', skipping over the oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר וְהִקְרִיב אֹתוֹ לְאָשָׁם וְהֵנִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The singular 'אותו' together with 'והניף' shows the אשם may be waved by itself.

steps.title: Maybe he should wave more than once
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that since the פסוק hints at both together and separate waving, maybe he should do both: wave, then wave again.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think he should wave, then go back and wave again?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistaken idea: maybe both readings of the פסוק mean he has to do several wavings. This sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural 'אותם' points to waving together, and the singular 'אותו' points to waving separately. One could think the פסוק wants both, which would mean waving more than one time.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think (introduces a possible wrong idea)
And go back (and repeat)

steps.confusionAlert: 'יכול' is not the final הלכה. It is a possibility the ברייתא brings up only so it can reject it.

phrases.english: One might think he should wave, then go back and wave again?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible conclusion from combining the two readings in steps 16 and 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the two readings require repeated wavings.

steps.title: Only one waving
steps.stepSummary: The singular word 'תנופה', not 'תנופות', shows there is only one waving.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'a wave offering', and not wave offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the idea of many wavings by pointing to the singular word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'תנופה', one waving. So he waves once, either both items together (the ideal) or each one alone. He does not repeat the waving.

keyTerms.meaning: Wavings (plural)

steps.whatToRemember: The אשם מצורע and its oil are ideally waved together, waving each alone is still valid, and the waving is done only once.

phrases.english: The verse says "a wave offering,"
and not wave offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers and rejects the suggestion of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The singular 'תנופה' limits it to a single waving.

steps.title: Before ה׳ means the east side
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: 'לפני ה׳' teaches that the waving may be done on the east side of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Before ה׳' means in the east.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא about the מצורע's אשם and oil keeps going. It learns from 'לפני ה׳' that the waving can be done on the east side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 16-20 settled how the waving is done: together or separately, and only once. Now the ברייתא tells us where it is done. This matches the משנה, which places the waving in the east.

keyTerms.meaning: Before ה׳; a phrase that tells us where something is done
East

phrases.english: 'Before ה׳': in the east.
phrases.notes: The פסוק about waving the מצורע's offerings: ויקרא 14:12.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, moving from how the waving is done to where it is done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Waving 'before ה׳' may be done on the east side of the מזבח.

steps.title: But elsewhere before ה׳ was read as the west
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this: another ברייתא said 'לפני ה׳' might mean the west.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't that other ברייתא say that 'before ה׳' might mean the west?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading that 'לפני ה׳' means the east. It points to an earlier ברייתא about a מנחה that read the same words as pointing west.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same phrase seems to mean two opposite directions. The west faces the היכל, so it seems more 'before ה׳' than the east. If 'לפני ה׳' means the west, how can our ברייתא read it as the east?

keyTerms.meaning: West, the side facing the היכל
One might have thought

phrases.english: But didn't he say:
phrases.notes: This points back to an earlier ברייתא about bringing a מנחה near the מזבח, which reads ויקרא 6:7.

phrases.english: 'Before ה׳': one might think it means in the west!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 21's reading of 'לפני ה׳' as the east.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'לפני ה׳' as the east side.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא treats 'לפני ה׳' as the west, which contradicts reading the same words as the east.

steps.title: The west applies only to a מנחה, which needs a יסוד
steps.stepSummary: The answer: a מנחה is called a חטאת, and a חטאת needs a יסוד. The southeast corner had no יסוד, so the מנחה goes southwest. For the מצורע, any side counts as 'לפני ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: that rule is only for a מנחה, which is called a חטאת. A חטאת needs a base, and the southeast corner had no base. But here, we call any side 'before ה׳'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The west reading was a special rule for a מנחה only, so for the מצורע's waving the east also counts as 'before ה׳'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'לפני ה׳' does not have to mean the west. A מנחה is compared to a חטאת, and a חטאת needs a יסוד, so the מנחה had to be brought where there is a יסוד. Since the southeast corner had none, the מנחה was pushed to the southwest. Without that special reason, any side, including the east, is 'before ה׳'.

keyTerms.meaning: A flour offering
A sin offering; a מנחה is compared to it
The base of the מזבח
The southeast corner of the מזבח
We can call it, the words apply to it

steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say 'לפני ה׳' means the west. The מנחה went west only because it needed a יסוד, and the southeast corner had none.

phrases.english: They say:
This applies only to a meal offering,
which is called a 'sin offering',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:10 says the מנחה is like a חטאת.

phrases.english: and a sin offering requires the base,
and the southeast corner
did not have a base,
but here,
phrases.notes: Here means the מצורע's אשם and oil.

phrases.english: we call it 'before ה׳'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 22 by limiting the west reading to a מנחה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the other source to a special case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzMaskana: The west is needed only for a מנחה because it needs a יסוד. Otherwise, any side, including the east, is 'לפני ה׳'.
steps.whyThisMatters: It confirms the משנה's ruling that the מצורע's waving may be done in the east.

steps.title: משנה: ביכורים follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that ביכורים need waving according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the first fruits, according to the words of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about ביכורים. This quote is setting up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists ביכורים among the items that need תנופה. It says this follows the view of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, but it does not tell us where his view comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: First fruits brought to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And the first fruits,
according to the words of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַבִּכּוּרִים כְּדִבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic from the משנה, about ביכורים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ביכורים require תנופה, according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.title: Which statement of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which teaching of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב the משנה means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the statement of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where we find this view of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה points to his opinion without quoting it. The גמרא wants to find the actual source.

keyTerms.meaning: What is

phrases.english: What is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opinion quoted in Step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The actual teaching of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב that the משנה refers to.

steps.title: The ברייתא: 'ולקח הכהן' teaches waving for ביכורים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learned from 'ולקח הכהן' that ביכורים need תנופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'And the כהן shall take' teaches that the first fruits need waving. These are the words of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a ברייתא. In it, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learns waving for ביכורים from the words 'ולקח הכהן'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says the כהן takes the basket and does not mention waving. That makes it unclear how waving is learned from it, which leads to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: And the כהן shall take
They require waving

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
'And the priest shall take',
taught about the first fruits
that they require waving;
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 25 by quoting the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא in which רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learns from 'ולקח הכהן' that ביכורים require תנופה.

steps.title: Why does 'ולקח הכהן' mean waving?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, since the פסוק does not mention waving.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר בן יעקב gets waving out of a פסוק that only talks about taking. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ולקח הכהן' describe taking the basket, not waving it. The גמרא needs to find the link that turns taking into waving.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the source in Step 26 works.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How 'ולקח הכהן' teaches that ביכורים need waving.

steps.title: A גזירה שוה of 'hand' from שלמים
steps.stepSummary: He learns a גזירה שוה from the word 'יד' in ביכורים and the word 'ידיו' in שלמים. Since שלמים are waved, ביכורים are waved too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns 'hand' and 'hand' from שלמים. Here it is written, 'And the כהן shall take the basket from your hand', and there it is written, 'His hands shall bring it'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the source: a גזירה שוה. The word 'hand' appears both by ביכורים and by שלמים, and שלמים need תנופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By שלמים, the פסוק says 'his hands shall bring it' and then speaks about waving it. Because ביכורים also use the word 'hand', they share the same rule of תנופה. This explains how a פסוק about taking can teach waving.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns, by comparing words
'Hand' and 'hand', the shared word in the גזירה שוה
Peace offerings, which are waved
Basket

steps.whatToRemember: ביכורים need תנופה according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. He learns it from a גזירה שוה: 'hand' by ביכורים and 'hand' by שלמים, which are waved.

phrases.english: He derives 'hand' and 'hand' from peace offerings,
it is written here
'And the priest shall take the basket from your hand',
and it is written there
'His hands shall bring it'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:30. The same פסוק goes on to speak about waving the offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 27 with a גזירה שוה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of 'יד' from שלמים, which require תנופה, so ביכורים require תנופה too.
